title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome
summary: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne as emperor of the Romans in St. Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day.
reason: Charlemagne had protected the pope from his enemies in Rome and ruled most of Western Europe, while the throne in Constantinople was held by a woman, Irene.
significance: It revived the idea of a Western empire and led to the Holy Roman Empire.
place: Old St. Peter's Basilica, Rome, Vatican City
